rows.line: We identify the Euler product as the structural component whose removal, in every family tested here, lets zeros leave the critical line. Epstein zeta functions, built from the same analytic pipeline as the Riemann zeta function (quadratic form → theta function → Mellin transform), satisfy functional equations but generically lack Euler products. They have infinitely many off-line zeros (Davenport–Heilbronn 1936). The Davenport–Heilbronn function provides corroboration: a different construction, the same structural deficit, the same outcome. Across all tested cases — Riemann, Dirichlet, Hecke, automorphic, Epstein, Davenport–Heilbronn, random Dirichlet series — the record is perfect: every tested function with both properties has all its computed zeros on the line; every function lacking the Euler product does not. In the language of proof by exhaustion, this experiment identifies which structural component confines zeros by exhibiting what happens when that component is removed.

rows.new: This paper compares functions that share the functional equation of ζ and differ in one structure. An Epstein zeta function of class number above 1 has the functional equation and no Euler product, and it has infinitely many zeros off the critical line (Davenport–Heilbronn 1936 in Re s > 1, Voronin 1976 inside the strip; classical, cited). At one member of the family, the principal form x² + xy + 6y² of discriminant −23, each part of the comparison is a theorem in Lean (SIDE-explicit-formula v0.41): the functional equation (`zq_continuation`), coefficients that are not multiplicative (`zq_coeff_not_multiplicative`), a zero off the line (`zq_offline_zero`), and the failure of Weil positivity on classK on the arithmetic side of its explicit formula (`zq_weil_positivity_fails`), in the form that for ζ is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (`h2_sign_iff_rh`). So the functional equation, the explicit formula and the local count of zeros, which this function shares with ξ, do not confine zeros to the line; that is compiled, at this one function. Across the families tested — Riemann, Dirichlet, Hecke, automorphic, Epstein, Davenport–Heilbronn, random Dirichlet series — each function with a functional equation, an Euler product and the Ramanujan size bound has all its computed zeros on the line, and each function lacking the Euler product does not; that is observed. Whether the Euler product is what holds the zeros of ζ to the line is not settled here: for ζ that statement is the Riemann Hypothesis, and it is open.

rows.new: Let Q be a positive definite binary quadratic form with integer coefficients whose discriminant is the discriminant D of an imaginary quadratic field of class number above 1. Then Z_Q(s) has infinitely many zeros in Re s > 1 (Davenport–Heilbronn), and for any 1/2 < σ1 < σ2 < 1 and T large it has at least cT zeros with σ1 < Re s < σ2 and |Im s| < T, where c > 0 depends on σ1, σ2 and Q (Voronin). Both are cited as Lee (2012) states them (relay `data/b751_literature.txt`, S1.c and S1.d), and neither is compiled.

### What is compiled at Q0

Each line below is a theorem in Lean about the Epstein zeta function of Q0 or about ζ, binding no premise, on the main branch of SIDE-explicit-formula at v0.41 (`a3aad4cc`); *The Epstein Control Object at Discriminant −23* v0.2 gives the statements in full.

- Shared with ξ: the continuation and functional equation (`zq_continuation`), the explicit formula (`zq_explicit_formula_instance`) and the local count of zeros (`zq_count_instance`).
- A zero off the line, in a box about 0.953 + 16.29 i (`zq_offline_zero`); 68 more stand numerical, to height 445.
- From that zero: Weil positivity on classK fails on the arithmetic side of the explicit formula of Z_Q0 (`zq_weil_positivity_fails`), where for ζ the same inequality is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (`h2_sign_iff_rh`).
- Lacking, where ζ has them: multiplicative coefficients (`zq_coeff_not_multiplicative` beside `zeta_isMultiplicative_control`) and nonnegative coefficients of the logarithmic derivative (`cQ_not_nonneg` beside `vonMangoldt_nonneg_control`).
- The same schema and instrument where the conclusion is true: two points on the line (`pc_online`), and a zero of ζ on the line between heights 12 and 16 (`zeta_box`).

For this paper's question, lines one to three say that the functional equation, the explicit formula and the count, held by Z_Q0 and by ξ alike, do not by themselves confine zeros to the line. Line four names what differs. None of them says that the difference is the cause.

rows.line: The sample covers seven function classes, each containing infinitely many individual functions. The record is perfect across all tested instances: every function with both a functional equation and an Euler product has all computed zeros on the critical line; every function lacking the Euler product does not. Across all tested function classes — Riemann, Dirichlet, Hecke, automorphic, Epstein, Davenport–Heilbronn, random Dirichlet series — the Euler product is the only structural component whose presence correlates with zero confinement and whose absence correlates with zero escape. No counterexample is known. The structural argument — that among the mechanisms tested the Euler product is the only one present wherever the zeros stayed on the line, as the discriminating-variable analysis reads them — supplements the correlational evidence. The Davenport–Heilbronn function provides corroboration: an engineered construction that removes the multiplicative structure and confirms that off-line zeros result. This is corroboration rather than independent replication, since the D–H function is constructed to lack the Euler product rather than being a naturally occurring object. The Davenport–Heilbronn theorem establishes off-line zeros generically; whether specific non-generic binary Epstein functions with class number exceeding 1 might have all zeros on-line is an open question that does not affect the discriminating-variable argument, since the point is that the functional equation *permits* off-line zeros while no tested function with an Euler product shows one.

rows.line: *Remark (The Ramanujan bound).* The Ramanujan bound |a_p| ≤ 2p^{(k−1)/2} on Euler product coefficients is a third structural ingredient. Epstein functions violate it as well as lacking the Euler product. In all tested cases, the Euler product and the Ramanujan bound co-occur — no known L-function has one without the other. A complete separation of their individual contributions to zero confinement is an open question. For the present paper, they are treated jointly as the multiplicative structure.

rows.new: *Remark (The Ramanujan bound).* The Ramanujan bound |a_p| ≤ 2p^{(k−1)/2} on Euler product coefficients is a third structural ingredient. The binary Epstein functions keep it and drop the Euler product: the halved coefficients of Z_Q count the ideals of norm n in one class, so they are at most the number of divisors of n. The shifted product ζ(s + c/2) ζ(s − c/2) keeps the Euler product and the functional equation and drops the bound, and its zeros sit off its centre line by c/2, by construction. So the record holds each of the two dropped without the other, with zeros off the line in both cases (relay `data/b726_mechanisms.txt` :9, :16). A Beurling system, which keeps an Euler product and drops the additive structure of the integers, was searched for one carrying a functional equation and a zero off its centre line, and none was found in the sources read (:23, :38–:42).

rows.line: The product formula ∏_v |x|_v = 1 is spectrally inert in the Tate construction (*Spectral Inertness of the Product Formula*, this collection): it builds the integration domain but introduces no constraint depending on the spectral parameter s. All zero-location constraints trace to ℚ's field structure — its additive group, multiplicative group, and distributive law. The Epstein experiment confirms this: removing the multiplicative constraint is the structural change that permits off-line zeros. The functional equation sets the stage. Removing the Euler product lets the actors leave it. In the language of proof by exhaustion: the Epstein experiment confirms that the per-class analysis (*The Seven Mechanism Classes of ξ(s)*, this collection) (in which each structural component is checked individually for zero-producing mechanisms) points to the same structural component, by exhibiting what happens when that component is removed. If the seven-class decomposition missed a structural force, removing the Euler product alone should not reliably produce off-line zeros — the missing force might compensate. It does not. The decomposition stands at this test. That no missing force compensates is the one open premise — the inter-class conservation step (named in five equivalent registers, *A Place to Stand* §27.3). The completing families of "The Complete Record" above (zeros confined) and the non-completing ones (Epstein, Davenport–Heilbronn, random Dirichlet — off-line) are catalogued in one grammar in the companion census *Paths to the Critical Line*, alongside two compiled negatives.

rows.line: The sample covers seven function classes, each containing infinitely many individual functions. The record is perfect across all tested instances: every function with both a functional equation and an Euler product has all computed zeros on the critical line; every function lacking the Euler product does not. Across all tested function classes — Riemann, Dirichlet, Hecke, automorphic, Epstein, Davenport–Heilbronn, random Dirichlet series — the Euler product is the only structural component whose presence correlates with zero confinement and whose absence correlates with zero escape. No counterexample is known. The structural argument — that among the mechanisms tested the Euler product is the only one present wherever the zeros stayed on the line, as the discriminating-variable analysis reads them — supplements the correlational evidence. The Davenport–Heilbronn function provides corroboration: an engineered construction that removes the multiplicative structure and confirms that off-line zeros result. This is corroboration rather than independent replication, since the D–H function is constructed to lack the Euler product rather than being a naturally occurring object. The Davenport–Heilbronn theorem establishes off-line zeros generically; whether specific non-generic binary Epstein functions with class number exceeding 1 might have all zeros on-line is an open question that does not affect the discriminating-variable argument, since the point is that the functional equation *permits* off-line zeros while no tested function with an Euler product shows one.
